Params: {3: 'The repeater replacement work out on the water is going smoothly.'}
{3: 'Now the group gathers in the hall at the base of the lighthouse and begins modifying the next batch of repeaters.'}
{3: 'The afternoon light slips in and softens the lines of their tired faces.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: "...You had to be there. The situation was critical. I've seen my share of close calls, but nothing like this.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The one with the impossibly long name holds court, spinning the tale of the storm they all weathered just days ago, embellishing every detail with gusto.'}

{2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: "So there we were, seconds from disaster, when 【kuroname】 here—quick as anything—grabs the captain's anchor and slings it across the deck. And guess who comes swinging up out of the water? Larsen himself!", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sava', 3: 'Yes! Exactly! I saw something go flying past and I thought, what in the world... then I realized it was Larsen!', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Larsen heaves a long, weary sigh, and the whole group dissolves into laughter.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'Hmm... if I reroute this here, it should handle the output cap for now...', 4: '1'}
{3: "Karenina's anchor weapon lies open before her, tools scattered across the floor around it."}
{3: 'After everything that happened at sea, you now share control of this weapon with her.'}
{2: 'Karenina, are you planning to leave my access to the anchor open?', 3: '31'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: "Wait, the captain's anchor can be controlled by someone else?", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sava', 3: "If it's the Gray Raven Commandant, honestly, that's pretty reassuring.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: 'Th-that was a temporary measure! Nothing more!', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "And what's that tone? You saying it's too much of a hassle?", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her voice comes out fierce, but the screw in her hand turns in the wrong direction.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: "What's wrong with the captain...? Is she getting… ", 4: '15', 17: '1'}
{1: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 2: "What's wrong with the captain...? Is she getting sh—"}
{1: '1', 3: 'Karenina rises to her feet, ready to put these two bold rookies in their place.'}
{3: 'In an instant, all color drains from the world like a receding tide, leaving only light and shadow.'}
{3: 'Then understanding hits. What Arius warned her about is happening right now.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'The anomalous crystals laced into those repeaters contain an isotope of Ytterbium-174, discovered by none other than your own grandfather, Kalon.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'It functions as a reducing agent. Within its "radiation" field, your M.I.N.D. will revert slowly... back into what it was originally designed to be: the perfect vessel.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'Each repeater you tear out, modify, or swap pushes your M.I.N.D. closer to its original state. The state of a perfect subject.'}
{3: 'The original "perfect vessel." What state could its M.I.N.D. possibly be in?'}
{3: 'Could there be awareness inside it? Could there be a soul? Would the world unfold before it in full color, or... in the absence of all color?'}

{1: '1', 3: "She remembers how Rarana's presence once calmed the whale calls in her M.I.N.D. But now, even with Rarana brushing against her, the green of the leaves in its glass is lost to her eyes."}
{3: 'That means... the strange force inside the little machine can no longer protect her from the "radiation" flooding in.'}
{3: 'But she cannot tell anyone here. It would only spark a panic.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: "You're all way too loud! I'm going outside. Get back to work, and I mean actual work!", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Karenina scoops up Rarana by its little claw and walks out of the lighthouse hall.'}
{3: 'Sunlight pours straight down from above. The beach nearby has turned a pale gray, and when the waves roll in, the white foam glimmers like a ribbon of silver.'}
{3: 'She draws a deep breath. Then even that silver line begins to slip from her sight.'}
{3: 'He extends his hand, and in his palm rests a small component.'}
{3: 'It resembles an external energy core, its surface traced with lines that shimmer with a soft glow as light plays across them.'}

{2: 'Larsen', 3: "That day, she put this backup energy core in your swaddle. The wind on the sea was so strong, and she was afraid... that if she couldn't keep holding you, you would be cold...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'We... made it to the rescue planes. Everyone made sure you boarded first.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'When we finally reached land and did the headcount, you and another child were gone.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'I always wanted to find you. To put this in your hands myself... Once I found the strength to face what happened.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'I was afraid the core would degrade if it sat uncharged for too long. So I kept it powered all these years.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Karenina just looks down at the small, warm piece in her hand.'}
{3: 'The colors have not returned. Her world stays gray and white.'}
{3: 'Her visual module seems to have failed entirely.'}
{3: 'Before Larsen can notice anything amiss, Karenina slips away again.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'Rarana... take me somewhere with no one around...', 4: '18'}
{3: 'An unfathomable black hole gnaws steadily at all that belongs to her.'}
{3: "It begins with light and shadow dissolving, the twin revelations of the world's face, now themselves becoming faceless."}
{3: 'By the final stage, whatever her visual module perceives can no longer find its name among her thoughts.'}
{3: 'Rarana leads her through the gaps between the reef rocks and up a rusted iron ladder.'}
{3: 'The launch platform sits tucked inside a hollow cave at the northern tip of Mirage Island.'}
{3: 'Rarana surveys the space and confirms it is hidden enough.'}
{3: 'The little potted plant still feels a stir of confusion, not knowing why this place seems so familiar.'}
{3: 'Karenina props herself up against the cliff face.'}
{3: 'The little potted plant drops from midair and presses its biosphere firmly against her cheek.'}
{3: "Inside, the holographic baby's breath shivers and rings like anxious wind chimes again."}

{3: 'Then it happens. One by one, as though someone is closing every door through which she hears the world. Her own breath vanishes first. Then the far-off cries of seabirds, the wind moving through the rock, the water washing over the reef.'}
{3: 'Door after door shuts in her face. Sound after sound cuts off, sinking into a silence that will never break.'}
{3: 'She clutches the little potted plant to her chest, praying it will work its magic the way it always has.'}
{3: "But the moment she holds Rarana close, Karenina's heart sinks slowly into the abyss."}
{3: 'None of the mimicked floral sweetness or the earthy scent of greenery from Rarana finds her now.'}
{3: "Arius' curse fulfills itself step by step, and her frame grows colder with every passing moment."}
{3: "Her fingers find Rarana's metal base, but the familiar rough texture of the material fades beneath her touch."}
{3: 'She sits in a vast, soundless void, a vessel being slowly emptied of everything it holds.'}
{3: 'Only the most primal instincts seem to remain in her.'}
{3: 'The world around her is vast and vacant. Maybe loneliness should be there, or fear, or... grief.'}
{3: 'To drift off course in a boundless ocean feels, somehow... only natural.'}
{3: "Rarana thrashes wildly, wriggling free from Karenina's arms and circling the motionless girl in a panic."}
{3: 'It pushes its scant computing power to the very edge of burning out, and still no solution surfaces.'}
{3: 'The spare energy component beside Karenina catches the light and gives off a faint glimmer.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Rarana picks it up with its mechanical claw.'}
{3: "Buried in the mechanical plant's deepest data are image after image of this same ritual—"}
{1: '1', 3: 'The young woman rotated open the base and slotted the spare energy unit into its internal port.'}
{3: "It was a soothing device Kalon had developed specifically to ease Cordelia's pain."}
{3: "Rarana unscrews its own biosphere. The metal base panel slides open, and its mechanical claw lowers the energy component into place. It's a perfect fit."}
{3: 'The moment the energy floods in, the stabilization program, which had been running in passive mode, kicks into overdrive.'}
{3: 'It plays the lullaby from the dream once more, and with it, the scattered fragments stored deep within this body.'}
{3: "As the stabilization program overclocks, a glimmer of life slowly returns to Karenina's eyes.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her thoughts gradually drift back into her body, though her vision remains nothing but black.'}
{3: "What reaches her ears is Cordelia's gentle humming, and voices from her memories, strange yet familiar."}

{1: "That's snow... the fish taste best when it snows. Mothers love making fish soup, but the kids all want it fried. Hot enough to warm you through, with the smell filling up the whole house.", 3: '45'}
{2: "That's snow... the fish taste best when it snows. Mothers love making fish soup, but the kids all want it fried. Hot enough to warm you through, with the smell filling up the whole house."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'White... snow... something warm in the air.', 4: '18'}
{1: 'Tropical forests are an endless sea of green, and the air smells like fruit ripening on the branch.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'Tropical forests are an endless sea of green, and the air smells like fruit ripening on the branch.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'Humid air... heavy with the smell of green. Green without end.', 4: '18'}
{1: 'The sand burns hot under the sun, with golden dunes rolling endlessly away. When the wind stirs, it brushes past like silk whispering against the ears.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'The sand burns hot under the sun, with golden dunes rolling endlessly away. When the wind stirs, it brushes past like silk whispering against the ears.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'The gold and orange and white grains... all sing together... They move like silk.', 4: '18'}
{1: 'The water is as blue as the petals of the loveliest cornflower, a deeper, richer blue than even the sky above.', 3: '45'}
{1: 'The water is as blue as the petals of the loveliest cornflower, a deeper, richer blue than even the sky above.'}
{1: "Wherever I end up next, I'll always find my way back to this blue.", 3: '45'}
{1: "Wherever I end up next, I'll always find my way back to this blue."}
{1: '1', 3: 'In her life as Karenina, the Engineering Force has sent her on countless missions to every corner of the world.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: "Cordelia... I've been to those places. I've seen them all with my eyes.", 4: '18'}
{3: 'The stabilization program slowly winds down, and Karenina exhales a long, steady breath. She tilts her head back toward the sky, and the tears that had not yet fallen are quietly soothed away.'}
{1: 'Tears shine like pearls under the moon, colored like its light, filled with the bitterness of sorrow.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'Tears shine like pearls under the moon, colored like its light, filled with the bitterness of sorrow.'}
{1: 'Red is blood. Red is fire. But red is also flowers and kisses.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'Red is blood. Red is fire. But red is also flowers and kisses.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: "It's the color of the sun... When the storm passes, the sun will bring a new day.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The little mechanical potted plant has saved her again.'}
{3: "Rarana may never be able to say Karenina's name clearly, but from the very first day it opened its eyes, it had been searching for her."}
{3: 'Rarana will never forget the day it finally found that name.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Hiding under a heap of scrap in the shipyard, it caught a conversation between two Constructs.'}
{3: 'Karenina of the Engineering Force would be part of this mission.'}

{3: "Its four mechanical limbs scrambled at a frantic, funny pace, and the waterproof white cloth draped across its body caught the dawn light as it flared outward, a child's dress lifting with a jump."}
{3: 'The air stuffed that "dress" full, the same way its "heart" was stuffed so full it might leap right out of its chest.'}
{3: 'It would finally meet the person behind that name.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Karenina straightens up and walks out of the shipyard.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Rarana pauses in the air for a moment.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: 'You want... a body? Like a human?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her voice is thin, still finding its strength.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "When we get back to Babylonia, I'll design a new body for you. And I'll... introduce you to all my friends...", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Rarana follows close, keeping pace with every step.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: 'Rarana, when a Construct switches frames, the designers try to keep the awakening sequence as close as possible to the way... human senses develop. In the same order.', 4: '1'}
{1: 'Rebirth begins with the body. Sensation floods her limbs, and instinct follows.\\nA hatchling spreading its wings, she reaches out, trying to touch something warm.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'Rebirth begins with the body. Sensation floods her limbs, and instinct follows. A hatchling spreading its wings, she reaches out, trying to touch something warm.'}
{3: 'She pushes open a door and steps into the temporary shelter. The bedroom sits empty. Everyone must still be at the lighthouse.'}
{3: 'Karenina sinks to the floor, releases a long, weary sigh, and lets sleep claim her.'}
{1: 'Smell comes second. A familiar scent lingers in the room, stirring a warmth she remembers in her fingertips,\\nand her own body rises to meet it, heat kindling like an answer.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'Smell comes second. A familiar scent lingers in the room, stirring a warmth she remembers in her fingertips, and her own body rises to meet it, heat kindling like an answer.'}
{3: 'Footsteps approach from outside the room, but exhaustion presses her eyelids shut and keeps them there.'}
{3: 'The girl lies on the floor beside your bed, her face bathed in the soft blue light that falls like moonlight across her cheeks.'}
{3: 'You call her name softly, and her lashes flutter in response.'}
{1: "The third thing is that person's voice, lighting the spark deep inside her.\\nGreat trees surge skyward, and waves roar forward, showing her the path ahead.", 3: '45'}
{2: "The third thing is that person's voice, lighting the spark deep inside her. Great trees surge skyward, and waves roar forward, showing her the path ahead."}
{1: 'And her single speck of starlight catches, blazing into a wildfire that swallows the heavens.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'And her single speck of starlight catches, blazing into a wildfire that swallows the heavens.'}
{3: "Your hand rests softly on Karenina's head, and finally, she lifts her gaze to meet yours."}
{3: "In the very first instant of her becoming, a gaze finds her. The commandant's eyes are on her."}
{1: '1', 3: 'The sea wind howls past Arius, catching the edge of his hood and tugging it back just enough to reveal half his face.'}
{3: 'Since his "resurrection," he has grown more and more comfortable in this face, this body, this soul, so abundant with strength and life.'}
{3: 'The stream of data feeding into the Sefirah grows thinner by the moment.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'In the end, failure is only a concept defined by people, interpreted by people. Nothing more.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The night deepens. Far off, a single point of light. Before him, a darkness so complete it cannot be pierced, only the ceaseless sound of waves devouring waves.'}
{3: 'The figure on the rocks stares into the darkness. Everything he has anticipated, everything he has been certain of, everything he has sought to seize, none of it has ever bent to his will.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'There is a certain pleasure, after all, in bending a will that believes itself unbreakable.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'He lifts his hand, as though he might trap the wind slipping through his fingers.'}
{3: 'The torrent of data has shrunk to a dry riverbed. The stream feeding the Sefirah is severed clean. It seems those people found a way to bypass the protocol entirely.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'What a pity... They could have fulfilled their greatest purpose by rushing toward me.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'How shall I define you? Understand you? Bend you?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'In his mind, Karenina takes her stance before that name, a protector refusing to yield.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'You really do take after him. Your dear grandfather, Kalon... The same infuriating stubbornness.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Breath must flow. Blood must flow. The hollow inside him cries out for the completed Sefirah, "writhing" without end.'}
{3: 'He needs everything to move. More agitation, more surging, more forward momentum.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The metal prosthetics folded behind him extend with a natural grace, rising to shield his eyes from the sea wind.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'This face was never meant to be leashed for long.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The waves grow louder, more restless. A reef long licked by the tide finally collapses, and with a roaring crash, more hungry swells rush in to devour it.'}
{3: "The disciple suddenly smiles. In his mind, Karenina's stubborn face fractures like porcelain, crumbling to dust in an instant."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'The "fruit" has ripened. If you refuse to walk the path of the divine, then you will serve your original purpose.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'My creation, I will put you to good use... and say my final goodbye to "that young lady."', 4: '1'}
{3: 'He gazes far past the horizon, something almost like admiration in his eyes.'}

{3: 'Beneath that lighthouse rests a hollow shell, reshaped by his hand through the Red Tide. If these people intend to use that lighthouse to hold back what belongs to him, then they must also be ready for it to bite the hand that wields it.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'What shall I call you? You who wished to become a monster. You who wished to find a home... Or perhaps...', 4: '18'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'The one who sounds the final note.', 4: '18'}
{3: 'The waves before him roar with the force of a full storm, seawater slamming against the rocks and sheeting down like a relentless downpour.'}
{3: 'The currents have been tampered with, the Red Tide hiding just beneath the surface. The storm has been gathering in the movement of wind and sea, and now it is fully formed.'}

{3: 'Its creator has released the reins of the storm. The tidal force drives the Sefirah engine, and he can feel the other half of the Sefirah, long asleep in the depths of the Atlantic Eye, beginning to stir.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'My dear child, the lullaby ended long ago.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The gale sweeps across the sea, and crimson seeps up between the waves. Grotesque sea creatures rise from the red, one after another, and surge toward the far northern node.'}

{1: '1', 3: 'Through the roaring storm, Arius keeps smiling into the dark. He lifts both arms toward the far lighthouse he cannot see, the curve of his elbows shaping a cradle fit only for a newborn.'}
{3: 'The wind carries the "god\'s" decree as it sweeps toward the island.'}
{3: 'The storm still lies far beyond the horizon, yet the sea has already thickened like dark silk. Though it is barely dusk, the water deepens until it swallows every remaining trace of light.'}
{3: 'Beneath the surface, a pair of hollow eyes are slowly opening.'}
{3: 'Those pupils flicker to life in the abyss, kindled by anguished cries.'}
{3: 'It wants to call out to something, but it does not know what.'}
{3: "It's important! It's important! <phonetic=She>It</phonetic> has to make that sound."}
{3: 'In those broken shards of memory, <phonetic=she>it</phonetic> once called out with such urgency, such pain, such despair, with everything it had.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Special Operative', 3: "Dr. Kalon, the service is over. We should move... You're scheduled for the lunar transport soon, and we can't risk anything happening to you here.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Special Operative', 3: "I've been briefed on the incident. What happened to your student... I'm truly sorry. But we are out of time.", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'A researcher in a white coat stood before a crab-shaped marine engineering robot, his features smeared into something unrecognizable.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Special Operative', 3: "This Corrupted hasn't turned hostile yet. We need to take this opening and go... Now.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'No one could hear it. No one could see it.'}
{1: 'No one could hear it. No one could see it.', 3: '60'}
{2: 'No one could hear it. No one could see it.'}
{3: 'There was no color, no smell, no sound, no...'}
{3: 'Its tiny frame suddenly shudders, and the rhythm of that trembling matches exactly the broken cadence of a human weeping.'}

{3: 'This hollow body was meant to rest eternally in the lightless void, unfeeling amid torment that carves like a slow knife. Instead, someone refined anguish into a burning charge and compelled the vacant shell to rise.'}
{3: 'It will wake everyone, only to mourn a loss already past.'}
{3: 'With that monstrous shriek comes a flood of data, rushing forward in wild disorder.'}

{3: 'The replacement protocol Karenina and the others laid down collapses all at once. The  "black hole," silent for so long, stirs awake and consumes everything in its path like an unleashed hunger.'}
{3: 'Beyond the reach of the lighthouse beam lies an endless dark. Waves surge out of that unseen blackness and hammer the shore without pause.'}
{3: 'But the waves are not the only things approaching.'}
{3: 'Alarms shriek across the entire island, unrelenting, pressing hard against every eardrum.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Lucia catches the anomaly at once from the readings, and the shadow between her brows deepens.'}

{1: '1', 3: "Twisted, grotesque, malformed shapes rise one after another from the heaving tide, their silhouettes sharpening as they surge endlessly toward the brightest light at the island's center."}
{3: 'Lee frowns at the data at the control center. There is no time to think. He jacks in immediately.'}
{3: 'Lucia raises her katana. There is no need for discussion. The act itself declares the judgment they both already share.'}
{3: "One last shared glance passes between them, and in that fleeting moment, each catches the worry in the other's eyes."}
{3: 'Has the protocol failure meant something went wrong for the commandant and Karenina? What trouble has found them, and will they make it through?'}
{3: 'The same fear grips both of them.'}
{3: 'Then, in the next heartbeat, resolve takes its place.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Lee & Lucia', 3: "(No matter what, we don't stop.)", 4: '1', 5: '2'}
{3: 'The brief calm is torn apart. The solid ground beneath their feet ripples like shaken cloth, and the sea boils in the lightless dark.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The terminal washes red, with alarms screaming without pause. Karenina pulls up the panel and runs through the data.'}
{3: 'The readings shift so violently that her expression drops.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: 'The protocol is breaking down... Data is routing back to the Sefirah?! Jormungandr... has a central node now? How the hell did he pull that off?!', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "Jormungandr was supposed to be a closed loop with no fixed central node. But one just appeared... and it's right under us.", 4: '1'}
{3: "Everyone follows Larsen's gaze. The lighthouse, dark for years and now repurposed as a Central Purification Filter, begins to glow from its base, light climbing floor by floor."}

{3: 'The moment it is fully lit, a deep grinding shudder rolls through the earth. The island starts to rise. Beneath their feet, the ground groans and fractures, sand and pebbles cascading down the shifting slopes.'}
{3: 'The island rises higher and higher until it hangs suspended in the air, revealing a metallic carapace utterly alien to the natural world.'}

{3: 'Seawater thunders off the edges of the mechanical shell in roaring falls, curtains of water plummeting onto colossal metal limbs. Bearing the entire island on its back is a gigantic mechanical crab.'}
{3: "No more than a few breaths, and the crab's metal back gives out a colossal, twisted howl."}
{1: '1', 3: 'Karenina slams the anchor into the ground, locks it firm, then grabs your hand and yanks you close.'}
{3: "The island's trembling surges, and then everything drops at once."}

{3: "When the crab's belly slams back into the seabed, the island bucks as if struck from below. The ground rolls in waves, hurling walls of water skyward. The sea floods in and swallows the island whole."}
{3: 'At last, every trace of violence is buried beneath the foam.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: "...I don't think it's ever going to be over.", 4: '1'}

{3: "One, two, three... Mechanical arms burst through the water's surface, their joints shrieking with the grind of metal on metal. They twist stiffly through the air and rush toward the island.", 4: '1', 5: '2', 6: '3'}
